source: NCERT Class IX, Democratic Politics I, Polity Ch. 1.

sections.heading: 1. What is Democracy
points: **Democracy** = a form of government in which the **rulers are elected by the people**.
Abraham Lincoln: government **'of the people, by the people, for the people'**.
It is contrasted with **non-democratic** governments (dictatorship, monarchy, one-party rule).

sections.heading: 2. Features of a Democracy
points: **Elected rulers** — the people choose those who govern them.
**Free and fair elections** — held regularly; the ruling party can be voted out; real choice between options.
**One person, one vote, one value** — every adult has one vote of equal worth (universal adult franchise).
**Rule of law and respect for rights** — the government acts within the **Constitution and laws** and respects **fundamental rights**.

sections.heading: 3. Arguments For and Against

sub: It is more **accountable and responsive** to citizens.
It improves the **quality of decisions** (through discussion).
It provides a peaceful way to **resolve conflicts** and correct mistakes.
It can be **unstable, slow** and involve much **political competition and corruption**.

points: Democracy is 'better than the alternatives' because it allows citizens to **correct its own mistakes**.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Democracy = rulers elected by the people; 'of, by, for the people' (Lincoln).
Features: elected rulers, free & fair elections, one person-one vote-one value, rule of law + rights.
In free elections the ruling party CAN be voted out (real choice).
Merits: accountable, better decisions, peaceful conflict resolution, dignity.
Democracy can correct its own mistakes — its key strength.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: Merely holding elections is not enough — they must be **free and fair**, with a **real choice** and the possibility of change.
**One person, one vote, one value** = political equality.
A democracy must respect **the Constitution and citizens' rights**, not just majority will.
Democracy's strength is its ability to **correct mistakes** peacefully.
